chapter: The House That Jazz Built and Homestead childhood
title: Pittsburgh clubs and being a girl
summary: She recalls the Leader House and Collins Inn but, as a girl, couldn't go to many clubs.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Do you remember any of the clubs. You talk about theaters and the larger places. I've seen reference to, for example, the Leader House, that's not German Lieder, that's
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

L-E-A- D-E-R, also Collins Inn. I recall the names of these clubs but I wasn't into clubs at the time. Most of the places that I would go to would be the public dances, you know, in the halls and the theaters because -- I certainly was old enough to go but maybe I couldn't afford to go.
Well, did being a girl make a difference?

Yeah, I think it did and not only that, these would be clubs that would be open late at night and I wouldn't be out late at night, because most of the dances would be over, no later than midnight or maybe one o'clock and I certainly would have to be home before then. Now, I wasn't a kid then, but for some reason or other I just had gotten the habit of getting out early and getting home early. I was quite old, I guess you'd say before I realized that there was something happening after one o'clock -- at night.
Okay, you've talked about some of the places you went to be entertained.
